title: Merge Sorted Array
statement:
You are given two arrays `A` (length `m`) and `B` (length `n`), each sorted in non-decreasing order. Either array may be empty and the lengths may differ. Produce a single array, also sorted in non-decreasing order, that contains every element of `A` and every element of `B`. Duplicates are kept, so the result has exactly `m + n` elements.

**Follow-up:** interviewers (Adobe, Razorpay) usually ask for the merge with `O(1)` extra space. A typical setup gives `A` as a buffer of size `m + n` whose first `m` slots hold the sorted values and whose last `n` slots are free. Fill that buffer from the back, placing the larger of the two current candidates at the last free position. The judge here only checks the merged output, not the space you use.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `m` and `n`.
The second line contains the `m` elements of `A` (an empty line if `m = 0`).
The third line contains the `n` elements of `B` (an empty line if `n = 0`).
outputFormat: Print the `m + n` merged elements as space-separated integers on one line.
constraints: A and B are sorted in non-decreasing order

examples.explanation: Repeatedly take the smaller front element: 1, then 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
A is empty, so the result is simply B.
All three copies of 2 are kept. After the 2s, 3 comes before 9.

complexity.space: O(1) extra (O(m + n) for the output)

hints: Both arrays are already sorted, so the smallest unused element is always at the front of one of them.
Keep one pointer in each array. Compare the two front elements, output the smaller and advance that pointer.
When one array runs out, append the rest of the other. This also covers the case where one input is empty.
